dehydrated_text:
Today, I usually lend my money to entrepreneurs. But back then, there weren't entrepreneurs; there were kings and noble people. They needed money to fight wars. This is why there was a demand for gold. If I'm a king, I need to fight a war, often against my brother or someone else to control this territory.

The problem with this system is that the king could get killed, in which case, oops. More commonly, the king would declare, "Screw you bank; I don't need to pay you back."

So, there are many risks with this system. Over time, a system developed to mitigate or reduce these risks. What they did was create cartels, partnerships between banks throughout Europe, usually through inner marriage. If 15 million receipts wanted gold but only 10 million were available, another bank would cover the shortfall.

If a king decided not to pay back his debt, other banks would ally and kill the king to recover the money. This system is what we call central banking today.

Central banking controls the world today. The key to this system is power. Money can turn nothing into everything; it's based on power. Banks can print out money, so why do we have poverty? If we could give money to poor people, they wouldn't be poor anymore.

Why are people still starving even though there's enough food in the world? Because of scarcity. But banks can print money out of nothing, making money infinite. Why do we still have poor people then?

You all believe money is scarce, but I've explained that it's not. Money is a number; we can print as much as needed. Power has brainwashed you into thinking something untrue: that money is scarce.

Money is not scarce; it's infinite. You must understand this. Poverty exists because powerful people don't want everyone to share the same wealth.
